submitted.rationale: Index 24 (Co0.23Sb0.77) had the highest measured EQE, 0.0212%. That is about 4x the stoichiometric CoSb2O6 trirutile (index 20) and about 6x the Co-rich spinel region (index 5). EQE rose toward the Sb-rich side, which fits a CoSb2O6 plus Sb-oxide mixture.

rejected.reason: Stoichiometric CoSb2O6 trirutile is on the hull but measured only 0.0056% EQE
The Co7Sb2O12 spinel region measured the lowest EQE, 0.0038%

consultations.verdict: Support: CoSb2O6 trirutile (mp-21908) is on the MACE hull (0 eV/atom), so index 20 (Sb 0.669, matching stoichiometry) should be phase-pure. MEGNet HSE gap 0.37 eV is known to underestimate for Co d-d systems; the gap is not decisive at 3.2 eV illumination. The known CoSb2O6 photoanode sits at this composition.

Support: the Co7Sb2O12 spinel is nearly stable (0.03 eV/atom above the hull) with an HSE gap of 1.44 eV, which absorbs well at 3.2 eV. This makes the Co-rich side, far from the weak trirutile, a strong contrast probe. Index 5 (Sb 0.208) is the candidate closest to the Sb 0.222 stoichiometry.

Weakly supportive, mostly uninformative: the Sb oxide (Sb4O9) has an HSE gap of about 1.1 eV, so it would absorb at 3.2 eV. An Sb-rich CoSb2O6 plus Sb-oxide mixture could perform better than stoichiometric trirutile, which beat the Co-rich spinel. The GP UCB also picks index 24.
